findings.title: SQL injection in migration via string interpolation
findings.body: The migration interpolates the host value directly into SQL: `execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, ...)"`. The `h` value comes from splitting the `embeddable_hosts` site setting, which an admin can populate. A value containing a single quote (e.g. `evil.com'); DROP TABLE embeddable_hosts; --`) will break out of the string and execute arbitrary SQL. Use parameterized queries or at minimum escape the value (e.g. `ActiveRecord::Base.connection.quote(h)`).

findings.title: before_validation crashes when host is nil
findings.body: The `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')` and `self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')`. If `host` is nil (which happens when the API receives a request without a host param, or when the record is built in tests without a host), this raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil`. The callback should guard with `return unless host.present?` or use non-bang `sub` and assign back.

findings.title: update action crashes when host id not found
findings.body: `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` returns nil for an unknown id. The code then calls `save_host(host)`, which executes `host.host = ...` on nil, raising `NoMethodError` and returning a 500. The controller should return 404 (e.g. `raise Discourse::NotFound` or `render status: 404`) when the lookup fails.

findings.title: destroy action crashes when host id not found
findings.body: `host = EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can be nil, but `host.destroy` is then called on nil, raising `NoMethodError` and producing a 500. Should return 404 when the host doesn't exist.

findings.title: Missing index on embeddable_hosts.host
findings.body: The migration creates the `embeddable_hosts` table with a `host` column but no index. `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host` runs `where("lower(host) = ?", host)` on every embed request. As the table grows, this will become a sequential scan. Add `add_index :embeddable_hosts, :host` (or a unique index to also prevent duplicate hosts).

findings.title: expandable_first_post? no longer requires any embeddable hosts
findings.body: The old check `SiteSetting.embeddable_hosts.present? && SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?` was replaced with `SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`. Since `embeddable_hosts` was removed as a site setting, the check now passes whenever `embed_truncate?` is true and there's a topic embed, even if no embeddable hosts exist in the new `embeddable_hosts` table. The method should check `EmbeddableHost.any?` (or equivalent) to preserve the original semantic that embedding is only expandable when at least one host is configured.

findings.title: category_fabricator.rb contains the wrong fabricator
findings.body: The diff swapped the contents: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines only `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while the category fabricators were moved into `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`. Although Fabricator looks up by symbol so the tests will run, this is confusing and fragile: anyone reading the file will think it fabricates categories, and any test that needs both will pull from the wrong file. The two files should be swapped back so each filename matches its contents.

findings.title: Combined @on and @observes decorators on same method
findings.body: `_focusOnInput` is decorated with both `@on('didInsertElement')` and `@observes('editing')`. The `@observes` decorator registers the method as a property observer, while `@on('didInsertElement')` registers it as a one-shot insert listener. Using both is redundant and fragile across Ember versions; the observer semantics differ from the event-listener semantics, and the focus call may not run when expected (or may run when not expected). Use only `@observes('editing')` or only `@on('didInsertElement')`.

findings.title: deleteHost action passed as a string
findings.body: The template passes `deleteHost="deleteHost"` (a quoted string) to the component. In Ember this is a literal string, not a reference to the controller's action. The component's `sendAction('deleteHost', host)` will fail to find the action and the host will not be removed from the list after deletion. The attribute should be `deleteHost=(action "deleteHost")` or the equivalent binding that resolves to the controller action.

findings.title: saveChanges action is unreachable
findings.body: `saveChanges` is defined on the controller but no UI element in `embedding.hbs` triggers it (only `addHost` is wired to a button). The corresponding PUT /admin/customize/embedding route and `update` action in `EmbeddingController` are also unused. Either remove the dead code or add a Save button to the template.

findings.title: Category referenced only by id, never re-hydrated in client store
findings.body: EmbeddingSerializer declares `has_many :embeddable_hosts, embed: :ids`, and EmbeddableHostSerializer exposes only `category_id`. The Ember side hydrates `category_id` into a `category` object only when the response has `__rest_serializer: "1"` and a `categories` collection in the root. `EmbeddingController#show` passes `rest_serializer: true` but does not include a `categories` collection, so `category` may be undefined on the client even though the controller template renders `{{category-badge host.category}}`. Verify the categories collection is included in the embedding payload, or have the client fetch the category separately.

findings.title: Uncategorized fallback is silently forced for blank category_id
findings.body: `host.category_id = SiteSetting.uncategorized_category_id if host.category_id.blank?` overwrites an explicitly blank choice with the uncategorized bucket, which may not be what the admin intended. If `SiteSetting.allow_uncategorized_topics` is false (and an admin chose none), this still creates a host pointing at the uncategorized category and the embedded topic will be rejected by the topic validation. Should reject the request with a validation error instead, or require a non-blank category.

findings.title: Controller spec has no coverage of create/update/destroy
findings.body: The only assertion is `expect(Admin::EmbeddableHostsController < Admin::AdminController).to eq(true)`. There is no test exercising the create, update, or destroy actions, the `ensure_staff` before filter, the SQL-injection-prone `host.host = params[:...]` mass-assignment, or the not-found path. Given the bugs in those actions (nil host on update/destroy), a regression here would not be caught.

findings.title: Embedding controller spec has no coverage of show/update
findings.body: Same as the embeddable_hosts controller: only a parent-class check. No tests verify the serialized payload, staff enforcement, or the `fetch_embedding` ordering.

findings.title: resources :embeddable_hosts exposes undefined show and index actions
findings.body: `resources :embeddable_hosts, constraints: AdminConstraint.new` generates index, show, create, update, and destroy routes. The controller implements only create, update, and destroy. Requests to GET /admin/embeddable_hosts or GET /admin/embeddable_hosts/:id will hit `index`/`show` and raise `ActionController::UrlGenerationError` or `UnknownAction`. Either add `only: [:create, :update, :destroy]` to the route or implement the missing actions.

findings.title: Removal of SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host? breaks plugins/clients
findings.body: The `allows_embeddable_host?` class method was deleted in this PR. Any plugin, theme, or external integration that called it (it is a public class method on a widely used model) will get `NoMethodError` after upgrade. If the goal is to migrate to the new model, keep a deprecated shim that delegates to `EmbeddableHost.host_allowed?` for at least one release cycle.
